name: Taj Mahal
tagline: 17th-century white marble mausoleum and UNESCO World Heritage Site
description: Commissioned in 1631 by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan for his wife Mumtaz Mahal. Built with ivory-white marble on the south bank of the Yamuna River, featuring extensive Mughal gardens and reflecting pools.

closed_days: Friday (Open only for registered Friday prayers at Mosque)
opening_hours.source: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) Official Agra Circle

entry_fee.children_under_15: Free entry with zero-value online ticket
entry_fee.ticketing_mode: Online only via ASI portal (No physical cash counter at gates)

visit_duration.basis: Security line (15-30m), garden stroll, plinth visit, shoe-cover queues, and exit.

walking_requirements.surface: Polished red sandstone pathways, marble plinth, garden paved walks
walking_requirements.shuttle_info: Pollution Free Zone (500m radius): Private vehicles must park at Shilpgram (East) or Amrud Ka Tila (West). Electric golf carts and CNG shuttles run to ticket gates for ₹20-50.

stairs.details: Ramps provide step-free access from Western Gate to outer courtyard and up to the main marble plinth. However, entering the inner cenotaph chamber requires ascending 22 steep steps or using an auxiliary metal ramp that can be congested.

elevators.details: No elevators exist in this 17th-century heritage structure.

wheelchairs.cost: Free of charge upon deposit of valid Government ID
wheelchairs.location: ASI Monument Office near West & East Gate entrance
wheelchairs.details: Grounds are paved and wheelchair accessible up to the plinth. Helper strongly recommended due to long courtyard distances.

audio_guides.source: ASI Ministry of Tourism Audio Odigos App

locations: Inside complex near Taj Museum (West garden)
restrooms.cleanliness_standard: Pay and use maintained by Sulabh International

drinking_water.details: Water RO kiosks available near security gate; carrying a personal transparent water bottle (up to 1L) permitted.

cloakroom_lockers.rules: Large backpacks, tripods, tobacco, and food items prohibited; lockers available at gate for nominal fee.

parking.location: Shilpgram (East Gate Parking, 1 km away) or Amrud Ka Tila (West Gate Parking, 1.1 km away)

transit.nearest_airport: Agra Airport (Kheria AGR, 12 km) or Delhi IGI (230 km, 3.5 hrs via Yamuna Expressway)
transit.local_transport: Pre-paid auto-rickshaws, app cabs (Uber/Ola), electric feeder buses.

crowd_profile.quietest_hours: 11:30 - 14:00 (Note: Marble floor gets hot in summer afternoons)

verified_disruptions.title: Strict Friday Closure
verified_disruptions.detail: Monument is completely closed for tourists every Friday. Only registered worshippers are allowed at the Mosque for afternoon prayers.

verified_disruptions.title: Drone and Tripod Ban
verified_disruptions.detail: Cameras allowed, but tripods, drones, external microphones, and power banks over 20,000mAh are strictly confiscated at baggage scanner.

unverified_aspects: Shoe cover dispenser wait times on holiday weekends (carry your own clean socks)
Night viewing slots (only 5 nights around full moon, tickets must be collected 24h prior in person at ASI Agra)

name: Qutub Minar & Mehrauli Archaeological Complex
tagline: 73-meter victory tower and historic Delhi Sultanate monuments
description: Begun in 1192 by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, the Qutub Minar is the world's tallest brick minaret. The complex includes the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque and the 4th-century rust-resistant Iron Pillar of Chandragupta II.

opening_hours.source: Delhi Circle, Archaeological Survey of India

entry_fee.ticketing_mode: Online via ASI website or on-site QR code scanner

visit_duration.basis: Monument circuit, Quwwat-ul-Islam courtyard, Iron Pillar, and Ala'i Minar grounds.

walking_requirements.surface: Level stone walkways and paved grass lawn edges; well-maintained by ASI.
walking_requirements.shuttle_info: Not needed; entrance gate is within 50m of main drop-off point.

stairs.details: Walkways throughout the lawn complex have gentle ramps. The interior staircase of the Minar itself has been permanently closed to all visitors since 1981 for safety.

elevators.details: Ground-level open air monument; no elevators required or present.

wheelchairs.cost: Free upon request at ticket verification gate
wheelchairs.details: One of Delhi's most wheelchair-accessible historical heritage complexes with ramped transitions.

audio_guides.source: Audio Odigos and ASI Signage QR

drinking_water.details: Chilled filtered water taps available near garden pathway.

cloakroom_lockers.rules: Cloakroom available at security counter for baggage.

parking.location: Designated DMRC & ASI multi-level parking across the road (approx. 150m walking)

transit.nearest_railway: Hazrat Nizamuddin (14 km) / New Delhi (17 km)
transit.nearest_airport: Indira Gandhi International Airport (DEL, 11 km / 25 mins)
transit.local_transport: Delhi Metro Yellow Line (Qutab Minar Metro Station is 1.5 km away, feeder e-rickshaws ₹10-20 to gate).

verified_disruptions.title: Minar Tower Interior Closed
verified_disruptions.detail: Climbing inside the Qutub Minar tower is permanently banned for all tourists. Viewing is strictly from the expansive ground courtyard.

unverified_aspects: Night illumination timings during monsoon weather or heavy rain days

name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
tagline: Historic Dravidian temple complex with 14 monumental gopurams
description: Dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi (Parvati) and Sundareswarar (Shiva), dating back over 2,500 years with present major structures built between 1623 and 1655. Celebrated for its Hall of Thousand Pillars and towering multi-tiered gopurams.

opening_hours.schedule: Morning: 05:00 to 12:30 | Evening: 16:00 to 22:00 (Sanctum closes mid-day 12:30 to 16:00)
closed_days: Open every day (Festival days have altered darshan schedules)

visit_duration.basis: Queue for security, barefoot walking through vast stone prakarams, sanctum darshan line, and Thousand Pillar Hall museum.

walking_requirements.surface: Barefoot stone floors (can become hot in midday sun; coir runners placed on main routes)
walking_requirements.shuttle_info: Vehicles restricted within 200m perimeter around temple towers.
walking_requirements.source: Madurai City Traffic Police & Temple Trust

stairs.details: Several raised granite thresholds (10-25 cm height) and steps entering the inner sanctums. Thousand Pillar Hall has stepped entrance.

elevators.details: Ancient religious granite architecture; no lifts.

wheelchairs.cost: Free with assistance assistance booth at East Gate
wheelchairs.details: Outer corridors are accessible by wheelchair, but inner sanctums have raised granite thresholds that require stepping or lifting.

audio_guides.details: Official temple licensed guides available at entrance; audio guides not supported.

locations: Outside East and West tower gateways in temple shopping perimeter

drinking_water.details: Purified water counters located inside the outer prakaram.

cloakroom_lockers.rules: Cell phones, cameras, leather bags, and belts are strictly banned inside temple. Official digital locker facility available at all four gates.

parking.location: Old Central Bus Stand Parking (Madurai Corporation, 600m away)

transit.local_transport: Auto-rickshaws, city buses, cycle rickshaws near temple streets.

crowd_profile.peak_hours: 07:00 - 10:30 and 17:30 - 20:30 (Also Fridays, Tuesdays, and Pradosham days)

verified_disruptions.title: Strict Electronic Device Ban & Dress Code
verified_disruptions.detail: Mobile phones, smartwatches, and cameras are completely barred inside temple premises per Madras High Court order. Traditional modest attire mandatory (dhotis/pyjamas for men; sarees/salwar with dupatta for women).

verified_disruptions.title: Inner Sanctum Non-Hindu Restriction
verified_disruptions.detail: Only practicing Hindus are permitted inside the innermost sanctums of Meenakshi and Sundareswarar. Non-Hindus can explore all outer prakarams, gopurams, and the Thousand Pillar Museum.

unverified_aspects: Special festival queue waiting times during Chithirai festival months (April/May)
Availability of senior citizen priority carts during heavy rush hours

name: Hampi Archaeological Precinct
tagline: Sprawling capital of the Vijayanagara Empire amidst surreal granite boulder terrain
description: A UNESCO World Heritage site spanning over 41 square kilometers along the Tungabhadra River. Features the Vittala Temple Stone Chariot, Virupaksha Temple, royal enclosures, and ancient stepped tanks nestled among dramatic rocky hills.

opening_hours.schedule: Monuments open 06:00 to 18:00; Virupaksha active temple opens 06:00 to 13:00 and 17:00 to 21:00
closed_days: Monuments open 7 days a week; Archaeological Museum at Kamalapur closed Fridays

entry_fee.combo_ticket: Single ASI ticket covers Vittala Temple, Zenana Enclosure, and Elephant Stables for the same calendar date

visit_duration.basis: Full day minimum recommended due to vast geographic dispersion across 15+ scattered monument clusters.

walking_requirements.surface: Uneven granite stones, sandy trails, rocky climbs, unshaded open boulder terrain
walking_requirements.shuttle_info: Electric buggies available for ₹20 each way between the main parking lot and Vittala Temple (approx 1.2 km).
walking_requirements.source: Hampi World Heritage Area Management Authority (HWHAMA)

stairs.details: Major sights (Matanga Hill, Anjanadri Hill, Queen's Bath, Achyutaraya Temple) require rugged stone stairs, rock steps, and uneven ground climbs.

elevators.details: Outdoor open-air archaeological landscape; no elevators.

wheelchairs.details: Zenana Enclosure and paved section of Vittala Temple can accommodate robust off-road wheelchairs, but 80% of monuments have natural rugged boulder barriers.

locations: Near Vittala Temple electric shuttle parking
restrooms.cleanliness_standard: Basic rural tourism facilities; sparse across remote monuments.

drinking_water.details: RO water kiosks at major ticketed gates; travelers MUST carry ample personal hydration due to dry heat.

cloakroom_lockers.rules: No centralized luggage lockers; travelers must leave large luggage at hotels or taxi.

parking.location: Designated parking at Vittala electric gate, Hampi Bazaar, and Royal Center

transit.nearest_railway: Hosapete Junction (HPT, 13 km, regular trains from Bengaluru/Goa/Hyderabad)
transit.nearest_airport: Jindal Vijayanagar Airport (VDY / Toranagallu, 40 km) or Hubballi (HBX, 160 km)
transit.local_transport: Hired auto-rickshaws, bicycles, mopeds (Anegundi side), rental private cabs.

verified_disruptions.title: Midday Heat and Sun Exposure
verified_disruptions.detail: Monuments have virtually zero shade canopy. Midday temperatures from March to June frequently exceed 38°C with radiant heat from granite boulders.
verified_disruptions.verified_by: Karnataka State Disaster Management / Tourism Advisory

unverified_aspects: Coracle boat ferry operational schedules across Tungabhadra River to Anegundi (subject to dam water discharge without advance notice)
Bicycle rental deposit policies in Hampi Bazaar

name: Kumarakom & Kerala Backwaters
tagline: Tranquil network of canals, Vembanad Lake, and migratory bird sanctuary
description: A scenic cluster of little islands on Vembanad Lake. Renowned for slow-paced houseboat cruises, Ayurveda wellness centers, and the Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary spanning 14 acres of lush mangrove wetlands.

opening_hours.schedule: Bird Sanctuary: 06:00 to 18:00 | Houseboat Day Cruises: 09:30 to 17:30 (anchored at night per fisheries rule)

visit_duration.basis: Morning nature walk in sanctuary or afternoon shikara/houseboat cruise on canals.

walking_requirements.surface: Level dirt and wooden boardwalk paths in sanctuary; seated cruising on boats
walking_requirements.shuttle_info: Boats dock directly at resort and DTPC jetty jetties.

stairs.details: Sanctuary walking path is flat. Boarding houseboats or shikaras requires stepping across a 30-50 cm gangway board; boat crews provide steady physical assistance.

elevators.details: Single level wetland and boat decks; not applicable.

wheelchairs.cost: Available at KTDC Waterscapes resort gate
wheelchairs.details: Level nature trails allow wheelchair transit for first 800m up to the watchtower base (watchtower itself has a spiral wooden stair).

audio_guides.details: Local naturalists and boat captains provide spoken commentary.

locations: Inside private houseboats (modern attached Western toilets)

drinking_water.details: Bottled and filtered water standard on all booked boats.

cloakroom_lockers.rules: Luggage can be safely kept in air-conditioned houseboat bedrooms or KTDC cloakroom.

parking.location: DTPC Boat Jetty Parking Ground, Kumarakom

transit.local_transport: State Water Transport Department (SWTD) ferry boats (very economical ₹15), pre-paid taxis, autos.

verified_disruptions.title: Heavy Rain Boating Restriction
verified_disruptions.detail: During intense monsoon weather warnings (Red Alert issued by IMD), the Port Department suspends small shikara boats and motorized leisure cruising for safety.

unverified_aspects: Exact migratory bird species counts prior to November season arrival
Real-time water hyacinth weed clearance status along smaller inner village canals

name: Amber (Amer) Palace & Fort
tagline: Hilltop Rajput fortress of yellow and pink sandstone above Maota Lake
description: Constructed in 1592 by Raja Man Singh I, Amer Fort is situated high on Cheel ka Teela (Hill of Eagles). Features courtyards, the mirror-inlaid Sheesh Mahal, Diwan-i-Aam, and panoramic views of the Aravalli hills.

opening_hours.schedule: Day Visit: 08:00 to 17:30 | Night Tourism: 18:30 to 21:15
closed_days: Open 7 days a week (Closed on Dhulandi/Holi festival morning)
opening_hours.source: Department of Archaeology & Museums, Government of Rajasthan

visit_duration.basis: Climb up to Suraj Pol, four courtyards, Sheesh Mahal, Zenana palace, and descent.

walking_requirements.surface: Cobblestoned steep ramps, sandstone steps, narrow heritage corridors
walking_requirements.shuttle_info: Jeeps operate from Amer town base parking up to the rear Chand Pol gate for approx ₹500 round-trip, avoiding the 800m steep uphill walk.

stairs.details: Major courtyards and upper palace levels have numerous steep stone stairways without handrails. The Jaleb Chowk can be reached via Jeep road, but upper palace access requires stairs.

elevators.details: Historic medieval fortress; no elevators installed.

wheelchairs.cost: Available at Chand Pol gate entry (deposit required)
wheelchairs.details: Wheelchair use is limited only to the first courtyard (Jaleb Chowk) and Diwan-e-Aam terrace via steep ramp. Inaccessible to higher residential palaces.

cloakroom_lockers.rules: Luggage counter available at main Jaleb Chowk entry.

parking.location: Amer town base parking (buses & private cars) or limited top parking near Chand Pol via narrow road

transit.local_transport: AC City Bus Route 5 from Ajmeri Gate (₹30), App cabs, Auto-rickshaws.

demographic_fit.senior_friendly: Moderate (Requires taking Jeep instead of walking hill)

verified_disruptions.title: Elephant Rides Strictly Capped
verified_disruptions.detail: Morning elephant rides up the fort are strictly capped at 5 trips per elephant and end by 11:00 AM. Government authorized jeeps provide the reliable alternative.

unverified_aspects: Light and Sound Show English commentary operational status during heavy monsoons (show is held in open amphitheater at Maota Lake)
Real-time jeep queue duration during peak Diwali / Christmas holiday seasons

name: Mysore Palace (Amba Vilas)
tagline: Indo-Saracenic royal residence with 97,000 illumination bulbs
description: Designed by British architect Henry Irwin and completed in 1912 for the 24th Wadiyar ruler. Features stained-glass ceilings, carved rosewood doors, solid gold throne displays, and the Durbar Hall.

opening_hours.schedule: 10:00 to 17:30 daily | Palace Illumination: Sundays and Public Holidays 19:00 to 19:45
closed_days: Open 365 days a year (Inner palace exhibits may close during royal Dasara rituals)

entry_fee.audio_kit_included: Foreign ticket includes multi-lingual audio guide kit

visit_duration.basis: Footwear deposit, guided one-way interior walkway, Durbar Hall, and courtyard gardens.

walking_requirements.surface: Polished marble and granite interior floors (must walk in socks or barefoot; shoes deposited at entrance)
walking_requirements.shuttle_info: Battery operated eco-vehicles available within the outer boundary perimeter (₹20).

stairs.details: Main tourist flow has gentle ramps up to ground floor halls. The upper Durbar Hall has an elevator accessible for seniors and disabled visitors upon request to staff.

elevators.details: Modern service lift is available to transport wheelchair users and elderly visitors between the ground floor and the first-floor Marriage Pavilion / Durbar Hall.

wheelchairs.details: Special indoor wheelchairs with non-marking wheels provided for palace interior to preserve historic floors.

locations: Near South Gate (Varaha Gate) and North Gate exit

drinking_water.details: Purified water dispensing booths inside garden perimeter.

cloakroom_lockers.rules: Shoe deposit counters are free and organized with token system. Camera photography is permitted in courtyard; restricted in specific sacred idol shrines.

parking.location: Large designated multi-bay parking lot outside Varaha Gate

transit.nearest_airport: Mysuru Airport (MYQ, 10 km) or Bengaluru Kempegowda (BLR, 175 km, 2.5 hrs via Mysore-Bangalore Expressway)
transit.local_transport: City KSRTC buses, prepaid autos, horse-drawn tongas for heritage ride around perimeter.

verified_disruptions.title: Palace Illumination Schedule
verified_disruptions.detail: The famous 97,000-bulb exterior illumination is active ONLY on Sundays, national holidays, and during the 10 days of Mysuru Dasara from 19:00 to 19:45. On weekdays, only sound and light show occurs without full palace bulb activation.

unverified_aspects: Special wheelchair assistant availability during peak Dasara festival days (advance coordination recommended)

name: Ellora Caves (Verul Leni)
tagline: 34 rock-cut cave temples spanning Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain traditions
description: Dating from the 6th to 10th century CE, Ellora is renowned for Cave 16: the monolithic Kailasa Temple, carved top-down from a single basalt cliff. Features 34 major monasteries and temples stretching over 2 kilometers of cliff face.

closed_days: Tuesday (Ellora is closed Tuesdays; note Ajanta Caves is closed Mondays)
opening_hours.source: Archaeological Survey of India Aurangabad Circle

visit_duration.basis: Kailasa Temple (Cave 16) takes 1.5h; Buddhist group (Caves 1-12) and Jain group (Caves 30-34) require walking or shuttle bus transit.

walking_requirements.surface: Basalt rock, natural stone stairs, uneven cliff terraces, open unshaded cliff road
walking_requirements.shuttle_info: MSRTC operates open-top electric shuttle buses between Cave 16 and the Jain cave cluster (₹20 per ride).

stairs.details: Kailasa Temple's lower courtyard is step-free from the main road, but upper galleries, bridge walkways, and higher cliff caves (like Caves 10, 11, 12, and Jain caves) have steep, uneven rock-cut stairs with no ramps.

elevators.details: Natural monolithic basalt cliff; no elevators.

wheelchairs.details: Main courtyard of Cave 16 (Kailasa) is accessible via wheelchair ramp. Caves 1 to 15 and 20 to 34 are largely inaccessible to wheelchairs due to rock stair ascents.

locations: At main entrance plaza near MTDC restaurant

drinking_water.details: Water filtration points at main plaza and near Kailasa complex.

cloakroom_lockers.rules: Cloakroom available at MTDC tourist facilitation center.

parking.location: Expansive MTDC / ASI parking area outside main gate

transit.nearest_railway: Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar Railway Station (30 km / 45 mins)
transit.local_transport: MSRTC state transport buses from Central Bus Stand (every 30 mins, ₹45), private tourist taxis.

verified_disruptions.title: Strict Tuesday Closure
verified_disruptions.detail: Ellora Caves are closed every Tuesday for preservation work. (Conversely, Ajanta Caves 100km away are closed on Mondays).

unverified_aspects: Exact electric shuttle bus departure frequency on weekdays between Jain and Buddhist groups
Flash photography restriction enforcement inside dark interior prayer halls (bring small LED torch for ceiling relief inspection)

name: Gateway of India & Colaba Waterfront
tagline: 20th-century arch monument overlooking the Arabian Sea in South Mumbai
description: Erected to commemorate the 1911 landing of King George V and Queen Mary at Apollo Bunder. Stands opposite the historic Taj Mahal Palace Hotel and serves as the embarkation point for ferries to Elephanta Caves and Alibaug.

opening_hours.schedule: Open 24 hours daily (Plaza security barricades may regulate entry 23:00 to 05:00)

entry_fee.note: Public open plaza; free entry after police baggage scanner

visit_duration.basis: Security queue, photo stroll along promenade, sea breeze, and adjacent heritage viewing.

walking_requirements.surface: Level paved promenade and stone promenade tiles
walking_requirements.shuttle_info: Not needed; plaza is directly accessible from Colaba roads.

stairs.details: Entire plaza promenade is flat with ramped entrances from security gates. Steps exist only at the water ferry jetties descending to boat berths.

wheelchairs.location: Paved flat plaza is fully usable for personal manual or electric wheelchairs.
wheelchairs.details: Paved sidewalks throughout Colaba Causeway and Apollo Bunder are accessible, though dropped kerbs can be intermittently blocked by bollards.

audio_guides.details: Self-guided or heritage walking tours booked via local operators.

locations: Public pay-and-use convenience block near Apollo Bunder bus terminus

drinking_water.details: Packaged mineral water sold by authorized kiosks along promenade.

cloakroom_lockers.rules: No public luggage storage at monument; left luggage available at CSMT railway cloakroom 2.5km away.

parking.location: Pay-and-park roadside slots on SBS Road or Regal Cinema circle; scarce during weekends

transit.nearest_railway: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT, 2.5 km) / Churchgate (2.2 km)
transit.nearest_airport: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (BOM, 26 km / 1-1.5 hrs)
transit.local_transport: BEST Bus Routes (111, 112, 138), Black & Yellow Taxis (Kaali Peeli), App Cabs (Ola/Uber).

verified_disruptions.title: Elephanta & Alibaug Ferry Monsoon Ban
verified_disruptions.detail: Passenger ferry boats from Gateway of India to Elephanta Caves and Mandwa/Alibaug are legally suspended every year from June 1 to August 31 due to rough Arabian Sea monsoon conditions.

unverified_aspects: Plaza barricade re-routing during VIP dignitary arrivals at Taj Mahal Palace Hotel

name: Victoria Memorial Hall & Gardens
tagline: Grand white Makrana marble monument and museum set in 64 acres of gardens
description: Constructed between 1906 and 1921 using the same white Makrana marble as the Taj Mahal. Houses 25 galleries containing rare oil paintings, historical manuscripts, weapons, and colonial artifacts.

opening_hours.schedule: Gardens: 05:30 to 18:00 daily | Museum Galleries: 10:00 to 18:00 (Ticket counters close 17:00)
closed_days: Museum galleries closed Mondays and National Holidays; Gardens open 365 days
opening_hours.source: Board of Trustees, Victoria Memorial Hall

visit_duration.basis: Garden promenade, Royal Gallery, Calcutta Gallery, portrait exhibits, and Queen's Hall dome.

walking_requirements.surface: Level paved asphalt garden walks and polished museum marble flooring
walking_requirements.shuttle_info: Battery operated buggies available inside gardens for elderly visitors (₹30).

stairs.details: Grand exterior podium steps have a gentle ramp on the North Gate side. Ground-floor museum exhibits are level and ramped.

elevators.details: Hydraulic elevator installed for visitors with mobility impairments to reach the first-floor Prince Hall and gallery exhibits.

wheelchairs.cost: Free of charge upon request at North and South gate ticket posts
wheelchairs.details: Broad walkways and ramps make Victoria Memorial one of Kolkata's most senior- and wheelchair-friendly heritage sites.

audio_guides.source: Official Victoria Memorial Mobile App & Audio Kiosk

drinking_water.details: Chilled filtered RO dispensers inside museum lobbies.

cloakroom_lockers.rules: Luggage counter available at main gate (no food, umbrellas, or liquids permitted inside museum galleries).

parking.location: Designated parking on Queen's Way and Cathedral Road outside complex

transit.nearest_airport: Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose International Airport (CCU, 20 km / 45 mins)
transit.local_transport: Kolkata Metro Blue Line (Rabindra Sadan or Maidan Station, 600m walk), Yellow Taxis, AC City Buses.

crowd_profile.peak_hours: 14:30 - 17:30 (Weekends see heavy family garden picnic crowds)

verified_disruptions.title: Monday Museum Gallery Closure
verified_disruptions.detail: The central marble museum galleries are strictly closed on Mondays. However, the 64-acre landscaped gardens remain open for visitors.

unverified_aspects: Sound and Light show seasonal schedule changes between Bengali and English time slots during winter months

official_sources.name: Victoria Memorial Hall Official
official_sources.type: Autonomous Body under Ministry of Culture

name: Pangong Tso & Chang La Pass
tagline: Endorheic trans-Himalayan high-altitude saline lake at 4,225 meters
description: Stretching 134 km across India and Tibet (China). Renowned for its shades of deep blue, turquoise, and violet water set against rugged arid mountain peaks. Traversed via Chang La Pass at 5,360m (17,590 ft).

opening_hours.schedule: Checkpost open daylight hours 06:00 to 17:00 (Movement restricted after dark by Indian Army)
closed_days: Road subject to sudden winter snow closure (November to April)
opening_hours.source: District Administration Leh (LAHDC) & Border Roads Organisation (BRO)

visit_duration.basis: Requires 5-6 hours driving each way from Leh (140 km) crossing high mountain pass; overnight stay in Spangmik/Maan or long 14h day-trip.

walking_requirements.surface: Unpaved gravel, stony lake shore, natural sandy terrain; NO paved walks
walking_requirements.shuttle_info: 4x4 or high ground clearance SUV required; strictly private hired taxis per Leh Taxi Union rules.

stairs.details: No formal stairs, but rocky, uneven scree and altitude make walking strenuous. Anyone with mobility limitations must remain inside vehicle or at lakefront road.

elevators.details: Remote wilderness mountain terrain; zero infrastructure.

wheelchairs.details: Extremely difficult for standard wheelchairs due to loose scree, sand, lack of paved walkways, and absence of medical lifts.

audio_guides.details: Local Ladakhi drivers and guides provide guidance.

locations: Dry pit / basic modern toilets at Tangtse, Durbuk, and Spangmik seasonal eco-camps
restrooms.cleanliness_standard: Basic high-altitude camping standards; freezing temperatures at night

drinking_water.details: Must carry sufficient bottled or boiled water; water freezes in shoulder seasons.

cloakroom_lockers.rules: Luggage remains in assigned tourist vehicle.

parking.location: Designated lakeside parking zone at Spangmik village boundary (strictly prohibited from driving onto the shore)
parking.cost: Free / Included in local taxi permit

transit.nearest_airport: Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport, Leh (IXL, 140 km / 5 hrs driving)
transit.local_transport: Authorized Leh Taxi Union 4x4 SUVs (Innova, Scorpio, Fortuner) or self-driven permitted high-clearance vehicles.

demographic_fit.child_friendly: Caution (Only for children over 5 due to AMS risk)
demographic_fit.senior_friendly: Caution (Requires doctor check for cardiac/respiratory fitness)
demographic_fit.budget_level: Premium (High vehicle hiring and permit costs)

verified_disruptions.title: Mandatory 48-Hour Leh Acclimatization
verified_disruptions.detail: By order of LAHDC Leh District Magistrate, all tourists landing at Leh Airport MUST undergo a minimum 48 hours of complete rest in Leh before traveling to Pangong Tso or Khardung La. High risk of Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS). Portable oxygen cylinder strictly advised in vehicle.

verified_disruptions.title: Mandatory Inner Line Permit (ILP)
verified_disruptions.detail: Indian citizens require an online Inner Line Permit (lahdclehpermit.in). Foreign passport holders require a Protected Area Permit (PAP) issued through an authorized travel agency for a minimum group of two.
verified_disruptions.verified_by: Ministry of Home Affairs / Leh Administration

unverified_aspects: Mobile cellular connectivity (Only postpaid BSNL and Airtel work intermittently; Jio 4G tower active in Spangmik but subject to solar power outages)
Daily pass condition at Chang La pass during shoulder months (October and May)

name: City Palace Complex & Lake Pichola
tagline: Rajasthan's largest palace complex built atop a hill overlooking Lake Pichola
description: Constructed over a period of nearly 400 years by 22 generations of Sisodia Rajput rulers starting in 1559 under Maharana Udai Singh II. Blends Rajasthani and Mughal architectural styles with cupolas, towers, and hanging gardens.

visit_duration.basis: Badi Pol, Tripolia Gate, Mor Chowk (peacock courtyard), Sheesh Mahal, Zenana Mahal, and optional boat cruise from Rameshwar Ghat.

walking_requirements.surface: Narrow stone stairwells, low ceiling passages designed for defense, polished tiles
walking_requirements.shuttle_info: Golf carts operate from outer gate to main palace ticket courtyard (₹50).

stairs.details: The museum route is a strictly one-way medieval defensive layout with dozens of steep, narrow stone staircases with low lintels. It is NOT step-free.

elevators.details: No public elevators exist in the historic museum structure.

wheelchairs.details: Wheelchairs can only access the ground-level Manek Chowk courtyard and Zenana Mahal open court. Inaccessible to the upper 80% of palace museum chambers.

restrooms.cleanliness_standard: Clean and well maintained by royal foundation

cloakroom_lockers.rules: Luggage storage available at Badi Pol main gate.

parking.location: Designated palace parking near Badi Pol (filling fast) or Dudh Talai multi-level parking (800m away)

transit.nearest_railway: Udaipur City Railway Station (3 km / 12 mins)
transit.nearest_airport: Maharana Pratap Airport Udaipur (UDR, 24 km / 40 mins)
transit.local_transport: Auto-rickshaws, app cabs (drop off at Jagdish Temple gate; narrow streets prevent large vehicles).

demographic_fit.senior_friendly: Moderate (Stairs can be tiring; courtyard is comfortable)

verified_disruptions.title: Old City Narrow Lane Restriction
verified_disruptions.detail: Large four-wheelers and tourist buses are prohibited from entering narrow lanes leading to City Palace between 08:00 and 21:00. Tourists must take auto-rickshaws or walk 400m from external parking gates.

unverified_aspects: Lake Pichola water level and boat jetty boarding ramp incline during pre-monsoon summer months (May/June)

name: Musée du Louvre
tagline: World's most visited art museum and historic royal palace on the Right Bank of Paris
description: Originally built as a fortress in the late 12th century, converted to royal palace and opened as a public museum in 1793. Houses over 35,000 works of art across 73,000 square meters of exhibition space.

opening_hours.schedule: Monday, Thursday, Saturday, Sunday: 09:00 to 18:00 | Wednesday & Friday: 09:00 to 21:00 (Night opening)
opening_hours.source: Musée du Louvre Public Service Department

entry_fee.ticketing_mode: Advance timed-entry reservation strictly mandatory online

visit_duration.basis: Security queue under Glass Pyramid, Denon Wing highlights (Mona Lisa, Winged Victory, Venus de Milo), and gift gallery.

walking_requirements.surface: Level polished parquet and stone floors throughout
walking_requirements.shuttle_info: Museum spans 3 interconnected wings (Denon, Sully, Richelieu) across 4 floors.

stairs.details: Major staircases (Daru Staircase to Winged Victory) have dedicated wheelchair platform lifts and bypass elevators nearby.

elevators.details: 18 elevators and 20 wheelchair lifts connect all exhibition galleries; iconic circular open hydraulic lift operates in center of Pyramid.

wheelchairs.cost: Free of charge upon loan with photo ID
wheelchairs.location: Assistance desk under the Pyramid (Allée du Grand Louvre)
wheelchairs.details: Manual wheelchairs, folding stools, walking sticks, and baby strollers available for loan.

locations: Every gallery floor in each wing

cloakroom_lockers.rules: Self-service touch-code lockers free of charge under the Pyramid (maximum baggage dimension: 55 x 35 x 20 cm).

parking.location: Underground parking garage at Carrousel du Louvre (Avenue du Général Lemonnier)

transit.nearest_railway: Gare de Lyon (3.5 km) / Gare du Nord (3.2 km)
transit.nearest_airport: Paris Charles de Gaulle (CDG, 28 km) / Paris Orly (ORY, 18 km)
transit.local_transport: Paris Métro: Palais-Royal Musée du Louvre (Lines 1 & 7) with direct underground entrance to Carrousel.

crowd_profile.peak_hours: 11:00 - 15:30 (Mona Lisa room has 30-45 min standing queue)

verified_disruptions.title: Strict Online Time-Slot Requirement
verified_disruptions.detail: On-site ticket sales are strictly discontinued during peak seasons. Visitors without a pre-booked online time slot will be denied entry at the Pyramid entrance.

unverified_aspects: Room-by-room temporary artwork rotation schedule (specific galleries may close without prior public notice for loan exhibits)

name: Sensō-ji Temple & Asakusa
tagline: Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple founded in 645 AD dedicated to Kannon Bodhisattva
description: Approached via the iconic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate) with its massive red paper lantern, leading through Nakamise-dori shopping street to the Five-Story Pagoda and Main Hondo Hall. Rebuilt after WWII with modern accessible infrastructure.

opening_hours.schedule: Main Hall (Hondo): 06:00 to 17:00 (Opens 06:30 Oct-Mar) | Temple grounds open 24/7 with evening lantern illumination

entry_fee.note: Completely free public religious precinct; optional incense/omikuji fortune costs ¥100

visit_duration.basis: Kaminarimon gate, stroll through Nakamise shopping arcade, incense purification, and Hondo prayer hall.

walking_requirements.surface: Level stone paving throughout precinct and barrier-free shopping street
walking_requirements.shuttle_info: Asakusa Panda Bus and Megurin community loop bus connect subway stations directly.

stairs.details: Main Hondo Hall has grand front steps, BUT has an elevator on the east wing that provides step-free access straight into the main worship hall.

elevators.details: Modern glass elevator operates on the east exterior of the Hondo Main Hall specifically for wheelchair users, seniors, and strollers.

wheelchairs.location: Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center across Kaminarimon
wheelchairs.details: Precision paved stone paths; tactile paving blocks installed for visually impaired visitors throughout the approach.

locations: Multi-function barrier-free public restrooms located next to Five-Story Pagoda and Asakusa Park
restrooms.cleanliness_standard: Immaculate Japanese public standard with baby changing and ostomate facilities

drinking_water.details: Purification water pavilion (Temizuya) for ritual cleansing; beverage vending machines ubiquitous.

cloakroom_lockers.rules: Coin lockers available in Asakusa Subway stations (Lines G & A) and Asakusa Tourist Center.

parking.location: Taito City Asakusa Underground Public Parking (Kaminarimon-dori)

transit.nearest_railway: Asakusa Station (Tokyo Metro Ginza Line, Toei Asakusa Line, Tobu Skytree Line, 200m walk)
transit.nearest_airport: Tokyo Haneda Airport (HND, 25 km / 35 mins via direct Keikyu-Asakusa Line train) / Narita (NRT, 60 km)
transit.local_transport: Tokyo Metro, Toei Subway, Tokyo Water Bus (Sumida River cruise pier 300m away).

crowd_profile.quietest_hours: 06:00 - 08:30 (Serene temple grounds before shops open) or 20:00 - 22:00 (Stunning illumination)

verified_disruptions.title: Nakamise Eating-While-Walking Ban
verified_disruptions.detail: By local shopkeepers' association rule, walking while eating food purchased at Nakamise snack stalls is prohibited to prevent spillage on traditional kimonos and crowds. Visitors must consume snacks directly in front of the stall.

unverified_aspects: Exact festival stall lottery layouts during Sanja Matsuri weekend in May
